## Breaking

### BUN144-BRK-001 websocket-close-handshake

- Section: `` ### `WebSocket` waits for the closing handshake ``
- Surface: WebSocket client, Bun.serve websocket.close
- Old:
  > It used to fire right after `close()` with your own code and `wasClean: true`, regardless of what the server did.
- New:
  > `close()` without a code sends an empty Close frame. Both ends report 1005 instead of 1000, including the `close(ws, code)` handler in `Bun.serve`.
- Escape hatch:
  > `BUN_CONFIG_WS_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` changes the 30 second timeout. `ws.terminate()` closes immediately.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-002 websocket-failed-connection-1006

- Section: `` ### Failed `WebSocket` connections fire `error`, then `close` with 1006 ``
- Surface: WebSocket client
- Old:
  > Before, `close` fired with 1002, 1007, 1009, 1011 or 1015 and an English reason, sometimes with `wasClean: true`, and often no `error` event fired.
- New:
  > A bad handshake, a TLS or proxy error, a protocol error, an oversized message and invalid UTF-8 are all reported the same way, like in browsers and Node.js.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-003 ws-package-node-parity

- Section: `` ### `ws` events match Node.js ``
- Surface: ws npm package (built-in)
- Old:
  > reason; // a Buffer, was a string
  > They used to inherit `Bun.serve`'s defaults: a 120 second idle timeout, a ping at 104 seconds and a 16 MiB limit.
- New:
  > An `'error'` event without a listener is an uncaught exception, like in Node.js. Add an `'error'` listener to every client and every server socket.
  > The default `maxPayload` is 100 MiB, up from 16 MiB.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-004 bun-serve-websocket-server-close-codes

- Section: `` #### `Bun.serve` WebSocket servers ``
- Surface: Bun.serve websocket
- Old:
  > Fixed: `server.stop(true)` closed WebSockets with 1006.
  > Fixed: `idleTimeout: 0` closed idle connections after about 256 seconds instead of never.
- New:
  > They now close with 1001 "Server closed".
  > It now receives a Close frame with 1002, 1007 or 1009 and a reason.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-005 glob-extglob-brace-ranges

- Section: `` ### `Bun.Glob` supports extglob and brace ranges ``
- Surface: Bun.Glob, package.json workspaces, package.json files, package.json sideEffects, --filter
- Old:
  > These patterns used to be matched literally.
- New:
  > They now have a different meaning, consistent with picomatch, minimatch and bash's `extglob`:
- Escape hatch:
  > Write `*[(]1).txt` instead.
- Upstream: [bfa1209e](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa) · PR: [#45043](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/45043) · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-006 pm-unknown-flags-rejected

- Section: `` ### `bun install` understands npm, Yarn and pnpm flags, and rejects unknown ones ``
- Surface: bun install, bun ci, bun add, bun remove, bun update, bunx
- Old:
  > Package manager commands and `bunx` used to ignore unknown flags, so this typo would silently run a normal install in CI.
- New:
  > Flags that none of these tools support are an error.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-007 pm-libc-filter

- Section: `### Linux installs skip native packages built for the other libc`
- Surface: bun install, bun ci
- Old:
  > Bun previously ignored that field, so every Linux install downloaded both builds.
- New:
  > Now it only installs the one that matches your system, like npm and pnpm.
- Escape hatch:
  > bun install --libc '*'
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-008 pm-peer-dependency-resolution

- Section: `### Peer dependencies resolve more like pnpm`
- Surface: bun install
- Old:
  > Before, the package got whatever version an unrelated package happened to install.
- New:
  > When nothing in your project provides a package's peer dependency, Bun installs a version that satisfies the peer range.
- Escape hatch:
  > Versions already in `bun.lock` don't change.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-009 tls-request-cert-explicit

- Section: `### TLS`
- Surface: Bun.serve tls, Bun.listen tls, node:tls createServer
- Old:
  > Setting `ca` alone no longer does.
- New:
  > Improved: `Bun.serve`, `Bun.listen` and `node:tls` servers now only request a client certificate when `requestCert: true` is set, which matches the docs and Node.js.
- Escape hatch:
  > For mTLS, set both.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-010 disallow-code-generation-strict

- Section: `` ### `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings=strict` only runs code that ships with your program ``
- Surface: --disallow-code-generation-from-strings
- Old:
  > `=strict` used to block a fixed list of APIs.
- New:

### BUN144-BRK-022 hash-rejects-file-and-nullish

- Section: `` #### `Bun.hash` and `Bun.CryptoHasher` ``
- Surface: Bun.hash, Bun.CryptoHasher, Bun.sha
- Old:
  > Fixed: `Bun.hash()`, `Bun.hash(undefined)` and `Bun.hash(null)` returned the hash of `""`, `"undefined"` and `"null"`.
  > Fixed: hashing an S3 file with `Bun.CryptoHasher`, `Bun.SHA1.hash()`, `Bun.sha()` or `crypto.hash()` returned the digest of an empty input.
- New:
  > They now throw a `TypeError`, and so do `Bun.hash.crc32()` and the other algorithms.
  > It now throws a `TypeError`, like it does for `Bun.file()`.
- Upstream: MISSING · PR: MISSING · Advisory: MISSING

### BUN144-BRK-025 fs-realpath-posix-semantics

- Section: `` #### `node:fs` ``
- Surface: fs.realpath, fs.realpathSync.native, fs.promises.realpath
- Old:
  > Fixed: on Linux and macOS, `fs.realpath.native()`, `fs.realpathSync.native()` and `fs.promises.realpath()` collapsed `..` before following symlinks, so `link/../y` resolved next to the link instead of its target, and `missing/..` didn't throw.
